business-domain-context

Business domain map: Validate Multitenant

What the product is for, how it earns, and what every domain term means. Source paths below are relative to the two sibling repositories: BE = ms_validate_tenant_backend, FE = spa_validate_tenant_frontend.

Overview

Confidence: Medium. The code is explicit about structure and rules; the business purpose is inferred from entity names, log shapes and the team's own test plans, because both READMEs are untouched templates.

Problem statement. Validate is a multitenant back-office for a biometric identity-validation service. The deployed system is the administration layer: a super-administrator registers client organisations ("tenants", identified by an Rnec code), gives each one its branches, terminals, devices, products, operators and users, and controls how each tenant may call the validation service (API credentials, a rotating secret, security thresholds, per-tenant log database) (BE/docs/Home.md, BE/MultitenantValidate.Domain/Domain/Entities/Tenant.cs). The word Validate and the log shapes (fingerprint formats, minutiae, scores, fingers requested) show the end-user transaction is a fingerprint check against a national registry operator (BE/MultitenantValidate.Domain/Domain/Entities/Logs/); that transaction runs in other components (a desktop "Listener", a biometric captor, the operator service) that are not in these repositories.

Target users. Three audiences use this admin panel, per the roles the code enforces (FE/src/app/core/auth/auth.store.ts): the platform's system administrators (Admin, the panel's "Dashboard / Tenants / Usuarios / Operadores / Productos / Configuración" menu); a tenant's own administrator (TenantAdmin, "Mi Panel": manages that tenant's branches, terminals, devices and users); and operational users of a tenant (UserApp, who only read their own tenant's logs). A fourth principal, TenantApi, is a machine login used by the tenant's systems.

Value proposition delivered today. Onboard a client organisation with its own encryption keys and credentials; organise its physical footprint (branch, terminal, device) and enforce uniqueness rules so a MAC, IMEI or serial maps to one place; control who may use it and how many failed attempts lock an account; let each side audit what happened through business logs (queries, requests, unsatisfactory responses) and generated ATDP documents; and keep an emergency "contingency" switch plus main/contingency operator per tenant.

Scale of the surface. 18 relational tables, 3 Mongo log collections, about 20 controllers, an Angular panel with roughly 13 feature areas. The team's test plan V2.2 covers 82 user stories in 13 modules (GEO, MAC, RES, BIO, SVC, AUTH, CONS, DOC, TOK, ERRBIO, NOHIT, LOG, ERRSEG), mostly describing the end-user biometric flow.

QA relevance

Business aspectTesting implication
MultitenancyEvery list/read/write must be isolated per tenant (IDOR checks across tenantId routes); the existing test report already probes this.
Biometric identity serviceData is personal and sensitive: encryption, masking, log content and retention rules are first-class test targets.
Operator dependency and contingencyTests need a controllable operator stub and the contingency switch; failover paths are business critical.
Account securityLockout thresholds (global and per tenant), rate limiting, token activation, password reuse history and secret rotation are rule-heavy and need boundary tests.
Bulk CSV importFour resource types import from CSV; malformed and duplicate rows need dedicated cases.
Spanish UI and error messagesAssertions should key on error codes (ErrorCodes.cs) rather than free-text messages, which are in Spanish.

Business meaning. A client organisation that uses the validation service. It is identified by a unique Rnec code and owns every other resource (branches, terminals, devices, products, users, credentials). Deleting a tenant is a soft delete.

UI labels. Create form: "RNEC", "Razon social", "Operador principal", "Operador de contingencia", plus security thresholds (see Tenant settings). The Dashboard shows tenant counts as Total, Activos, Inactivos, Eliminados. Labels are hardcoded Spanish in the Angular templates; there are no i18n bundles.

Related terms. Tenant settings, Tenant administrator, Application user, Branch, Terminal, Device, Product, Operator.

Abbreviations. RNEC (the code field; its expansion is not stated in code, see discovery gaps).

Business meaning. A request by a system administrator to export documents (PDFs) for a tenant and a date range. The test plan describes ATDP as a screen in the end-user flow that shows a blocked document; the admin-side meaning here is the export of those records.

Hit and No Hit

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTable / collectionFound in
Hit / No Hit (validation outcome)ScoreHit, HitTwoFingers, LogRespuestaNoSatisfactoriaNr"Resultado de Validacion de Identidad Exitosa - HIT" (test plan wording, end-user screen)Part of tenant JSON and the Mongo unsatisfactory-response log../PruebasMultitenantValidate/HU Validate/Plan de Pruebas Validate V2.2.md

Business meaning. Confidence: Medium (from team documents, not from code). A Hit is a successful biometric match; a No Hit is a result that did not confirm the identity. Repeated No Hits (or Hits) on one document can block that document, with a configurable limit. A technical error does not count as a No Hit.

UI labels. End-user screens are outside these repositories; wording quoted from the test plan only.

Related terms. Unsatisfactory response log, ATDP download, Tenant settings.

Abbreviations. NUT (a transaction number the plan says is not generated when a document is blocked; meaning unconfirmed).

Discovery gaps

  • Revenue Streams: Unknown -- requires user input. No billing or pricing code; how the service is monetised is not visible.
  • RNEC expansion: used as the tenant identifier and in the plan as "interpreting status codes reported by RNEC"; the full name is not stated in code or the files read. Ask the team.
  • ATDP expansion and meaning: backend calls it a downloadable document; the test plan calls it a screen shown when a document is blocked. Likely a personal-data-processing authorisation, unconfirmed. The plan itself lists "TDP vs ATF" as an open question.
  • NR suffix on the three log types: probably the registry operator side; unconfirmed.
  • NUT: mentioned in the test plan (not generated when a document is blocked); definition not found.
  • Role table versus effective access: access is decided by user type + policies; what the Role table is meant to control is unclear. The constant Administrador (named AdminSistema) has no confirmed use.
  • Table name mismatch with the backend docs: docs/Modelo-de-dominio.md lists plural table names (Tenants, Users), while the migrations create singular names (Tenant, User). Migrations were treated as authoritative. A live database check was impossible (dbhub MCP failed to connect).
  • Docs versus code on lockout: the V2.1 test plan says the lockout is permanent until an administrator acts, while User has a LockoutEnd field and root accounts a 10-minute lockout. Confirm with the team which is current.
  • Frontend labels without i18n: labels come from hardcoded Spanish text in component templates, not from translation bundles. Accents were not preserved here; confirm exact strings when writing UI selectors.
  • ATDP and contingency screens: the exact UI wording for the contingency toggle and any ATDP admin screen was not extracted; no ATDP feature folder exists in the frontend.
  • End-user biometric flow: the Listener, captor, geolocation and result screens in the test plan (modules GEO, MAC, RES, BIO, TOK, NOHIT) are not in these repositories; terms from them (Hit, No Hit, NUT) are Medium confidence at best.
  • Ignored source: VersionesBackend/ was excluded by decision; entities there may differ.
  • Frontend roles folder: FE/src/app/features/roles/ exists without a menu entry; whether it is live is unconfirmed.
